goals.label: Understand or research
goals.description: Explain behavior, recover design rationale, or investigate primary sources.

goals.label: Plan tests or verify behavior
goals.description: Choose testing strategy, write behavior checks, or build stronger verification.

goals.label: Clarify a plan or write a specification
goals.description: Resolve open decisions, synthesize settled discussion, or split an agreed plan.

goals.label: Implement agreed work
goals.description: Execute a bounded spec or its existing ticket graph.

goals.label: Diagnose a failure or performance symptom
goals.description: Choose a reproduce-and-fix loop or live diagnosis without a product fix.

goals.label: Explore or improve a design
goals.description: Get interface advice, test an idea cheaply, or design and implement the chosen shape.

goals.label: Review changes or prepare delivery
goals.description: Separate review findings, PR communication, merge readiness, and actually landing changes.

goals.label: Write clearly or learn something
goals.description: Choose a conversational explanation, persistent learning workspace, or technical writing support.

goals.label: Improve workflows or coordinate work
goals.description: Triage requests, learn from a session, prevent recurring mistakes, sharpen prompts, or partition work.

goals.label: Carry context into the next step
goals.description: Prepare a portable handoff or catch up on an active chat, including software work.

understand-focus.question: What do you need to understand?
understand-focus.hint: Choose the evidence you need, rather than the author you prefer.

choices.label: How existing code works and where behavior belongs
Why an existing design or decision exists
Facts about a topic, API, or external technology

test-intent.question: What testing result do you want?
test-intent.hint: Planning how to test is a separate task from writing or running tests.

choices.label: Choose a strategy for testing a module
Write tests while building feature behavior
Capture and fix a known bug with a regression check
Build or maintain checks that drive the real application
Check a costly invariant beyond example-based tests

module-execution.question: What execution is allowed for the module checks?
module-execution.hint: Not starting the whole application is different from not executing any code.

choices.label: Isolated tests may run; the whole system must not start
Analysis only; do not execute code

app-check-state.question: Does the project already have a verification skill and feature map?
app-check-state.hint: These checks launch and drive the real application. Use module strategy if full-system startup is forbidden.

choices.label: No; create a repeatable real-app verification workflow
Yes; audit and update its source and live coverage

plan-state.question: How settled is the plan?
plan-state.hint: A settled discussion should become a specification before implementation.

choices.label: Important product or design decisions are still open
Discussion is settled; write the specification
An agreed plan or spec needs verifiable tickets

implementation-size.question: What is already specified?
implementation-size.hint: Use planning first if the expected behavior is still unsettled.

choices.label: One bounded change, spec, or set of tickets
A whole spec with a dependency graph of tickets

diagnosis-result.question: What diagnosis result do you need?
diagnosis-result.hint: Live instrumentation and repository fixes have different action scopes.

choices.label: Reproduce a bug or regression, find its cause, and fix it
Diagnose a live runtime symptom; do not implement a fix

design-depth.question: How far should design work go?
design-depth.hint: Poteto architect continues to implementation by default; choose reference advice if that is outside scope.

choices.label: Advice on module interfaces and seams only
A throwaway prototype to answer a design question
Compare designs, then implement the chosen shape

review-result.question: What should happen after the review?
review-result.hint: Reviewing, making a PR ready, and merging it are distinct tasks.

choices.label: Report code findings against standards and a spec
Challenge a change with independent model reviews
Write the pull request description
Drive an existing PR to merge-ready; do not merge
Independently verify and land authorized PRs

writing-learning.question: Which result would help you?
writing-learning.hint: A short lesson and a persistent learning workspace have different scope.

choices.label: Learn through a conversational explanation now
Build a learning workspace across multiple sessions
Write or improve a technical document

improvement-target.question: What needs improvement?
improvement-target.hint: Pick the change you want, since some of these workflows only report while others edit and commit.

choices.label: Turn incoming requests into verified, actionable briefs
Find improvements after a coding session
Prevent the same agent mistakes from recurring
Improve a task prompt without widening scope
Coordinate bounded parallel coverage or candidates

context-action.question: Who needs the context?
context-action.hint: These routes also apply to coding projects; no software/non-software fork is required.

choices.label: A fresh agent or next session must continue the work
I need to catch up on this chat and its open decisions

explain-system.title: Explain existing behavior
explain-system.why: It grounds an architectural explanation in code, ownership, and runtime flow.
explain-system.next_step: Name one subsystem and ask for its entry points, data flow, owners, and important gotchas.
explain-system.boundary: This is an explanation. It does not authorize implementing changes.
prerequisites: Access to the relevant code.
An agent host able to support or adapt the source workflow’s explorer and explainer roles.

alternative.when: You want a conversational lesson that combines behavior and rationale.

recover-rationale.title: Recover the reasons behind a design
recover-rationale.why: It investigates historical constraints and explicitly separates findings from inference.
recover-rationale.next_step: Name the design decision and collect code anchors, source-control history, and any available decision records.
recover-rationale.boundary: Missing evidence stays a gap; plausible rationale is not a confirmed historical fact.
prerequisites: Relevant source-control history.
Access to any connected evidence sources to be queried; unavailable categories must be reported.

alternative.when: The real question is what the code does today, rather than why it was chosen.

research-topic.title: Research a bounded question
research-topic.why: It traces claims to primary sources and saves a cited research note.
research-topic.next_step: State the question, the decision it informs, and where the research note belongs.
research-topic.boundary: The deliverable is a research note, not an implementation or an unqualified recommendation.
prerequisites: A bounded research question.
Access to relevant primary sources and a writable notes destination.
Background research-agent capability or a stated adaptation.

alternative.when: The question is specifically historical rationale for code already in your repository.

module-isolated-strategy.title: Plan isolated module tests without starting the system
module-isolated-strategy.why: This reference owns interface and seam design for testability. Its dependency guide distinguishes in-process work, local stand-ins, owned remote services, and external systems.
module-isolated-strategy.next_step: Produce a testability map: the public interface, dependency categories, available stand-ins, smallest isolated invocation, behaviors it catches, and integrations it leaves unverified.
module-isolated-strategy.boundary: Consult this as a reference, not a coordinator. Planning does not authorize refactoring or writing tests. An isolated pass cannot prove the real integrations work.
prerequisites: Identify the module and its callers.
Confirm which local processes, fixtures, stand-ins, and network calls an isolated check may use.

alternative.when: You explicitly request writing tests, agree the seams first, and allow the required isolated execution.

support.when: Use only if ownership or runtime flow must first be mapped from code.

module-analysis-strategy.title: Analyze module testability without executing code
module-analysis-strategy.why: This reference supplies the vocabulary for choosing the test interface and classifying dependencies before any test is run.
module-analysis-strategy.next_step: Write an analysis-only testability map with candidate seams, dependencies, hypothetical stand-ins, proposed checks, and every assumption that still needs execution evidence.
module-analysis-strategy.boundary: Read and reason only. Do not run code or call the proposed checks verified. Treat this skill as a reference, not an execution workflow.
prerequisites: Access to module source, callers, and existing test examples.
A clear no-execution constraint.

alternative.when: Later, you request writing tests, agree the seams, and explicitly allow execution; until then it is not the next action.

support.when: Consult if an explanation of the existing code is needed to identify the seam.

feature-test-first.title: Build feature behavior one failing test at a time
feature-test-first.why: It targets observable behavior through agreed public seams, with one red-to-green slice at a time.
feature-test-first.next_step: List the proposed seams with what each catches and misses, confirm them, then write one independently expected failing test.
feature-test-first.boundary: Do not write tests at unconfirmed seams. Its current loop excludes refactoring, which belongs to the later review stage.
prerequisites: Requested test-first feature work.
User agreement on testing seams before writing tests.
A runnable focused test command and permission for implementation changes.

alternative.when: You are fixing a specific known bug with a cheap local regression target, rather than building feature behavior.

support.when: Reference when the interface or testing seam itself needs design.

bug-regression.title: Lock down a known bug with a focused regression
bug-regression.why: It requires failing-before and passing-after evidence on a practical local bug path.
bug-regression.next_step: Identify intended and broken behavior; choose the smallest existing executable check and show it fail before changing production code.
bug-regression.boundary: Do not build a broad brittle harness merely to add a test. If a failing test is impractical, report the closest executable proof and its limits.
prerequisites: A specific bug and expected behavior.
An inexpensive local test target, or an explicitly requested regression check.
Permission to fix the bug and execute the check.

alternative.when: The failure is hard to reproduce or its cause is unknown; build a reliable feedback loop before choosing the fix.

create-app-check.title: Create a repeatable real-app verification workflow
create-app-check.why: It builds launch, health, drive, evidence, cleanup, and feature-map instructions grounded in the actual repository.
create-app-check.next_step: Identify the primary user surface and existing harness, then generate the workflow and run one complete mapped journey.
create-app-check.boundary: This starts and drives the application and writes a project-local skill. A generated workflow that was never executed remains a draft.
prerequisites: Permission and prerequisites to start the real application.
A safe test instance, required configuration, and controllable user surface.

alternative.when: The full application must not run; consult the reference to plan isolated module checks instead.

maintain-app-check.title: Audit an existing app verification workflow
maintain-app-check.why: It compares each feature map entry with source and live behavior, then corrects proven harness or documentation drift.
maintain-app-check.next_step: Locate the existing verification skill and map, cover every mapped feature from source and live execution, and report gaps.
maintain-app-check.boundary: Edits belong to the verification skill and harness. Product regressions are reported, not hidden by weakening the map.
prerequisites: An existing project-local verification skill and feature map.
Permission and environment to drive every reachable feature live.

alternative.when: No verification skill or feature map exists yet.

formal-check.title: Create a scoped invariant verification workflow
formal-check.why: It chooses a tool for one costly invariant, ties the model to real code, and demonstrates that the check can fail.
formal-check.next_step: State the invariant and user harm, pick the smallest appropriate verifier, record assumptions and bounds, and test a deliberately broken variant.
formal-check.boundary: A pass covers only stated scope and assumptions. Report real product violations without changing product code unless requested.
prerequisites: Relevant source code and a meaningful invariant.
Permission to create local verification artifacts and run the chosen tool.

alternative.when: A formal workflow already exists and must be reconciled with changed code.

support.when: Use for readable TLA+ states and counterexample paths when a TLA+ model is chosen.

clarify-plan.title: Clarify decisions and preserve the domain language
clarify-plan.why: It combines a decision interview with domain modeling so decisions and terminology persist.
clarify-plan.next_step: Bring the proposal and constraints; identify answerable decisions and record agreed terms and significant tradeoffs.
clarify-plan.boundary: This sharpens a plan and writes relevant domain documentation; it is not an instruction to start implementation.
prerequisites: A plan or design to interrogate.
Willingness to answer product decisions and a destination for domain documents.

alternative.when: You want the interview without the persistent glossary and decision-document wrapper.

write-spec.title: Turn settled discussion into a specification
write-spec.why: It synthesizes what is already discussed into user stories, decisions, scope, and a test strategy.
write-spec.next_step: Read the settled discussion, sketch the testing seams for confirmation, and publish the synthesized specification to the configured tracker.
write-spec.boundary: This creates a specification and tracker entry, not implementation. It avoids restarting the product interview but still checks proposed testing seams.
prerequisites: Enough settled discussion to synthesize.
Configured issue-tracker and triage conventions.
Agreement on testing seams and authorization for the selected publication destination.

alternative.when: Material product or design decisions are still unresolved.

support.when: Configure the repository first if tracker conventions are missing.

split-tickets.title: Split an agreed plan into verifiable work
split-tickets.why: It makes vertical, independently verifiable slices with explicit blocking edges.
split-tickets.next_step: Read the plan and create demoable tickets with acceptance evidence and dependency relationships.
split-tickets.boundary: Ticket publication changes the configured tracker. Tickets are a work graph, not a substitute for implementing or verifying the feature.
prerequisites: An existing plan, spec, or sufficiently settled discussion.
Configured tracker and authorization to publish tickets.

alternative.when: The discussion is settled but still needs a coherent specification before slicing.

implement-scoped.title: Implement a bounded specification
implement-scoped.why: It implements supplied work with agreed test seams, focused checks, final review, and a commit.
implement-scoped.next_step: Supply the spec or exact ticket reference, confirm testing seams, then implement and verify the bounded change.
implement-scoped.boundary: This writes and commits code on the current branch. A recommendation does not establish that the source workflow is installed or compatible.
prerequisites: A supplied spec or unambiguous tickets.
Permission to edit and commit in the intended checkout.
Agreed testing seams and repository checks.

alternative.when: The work needs competing interface designs followed by implementation, rather than a settled shape.

implement-ticket-graph.title: Implement a specification across its ticket graph
implement-ticket-graph.why: It dispatches ready tickets into worktrees and integrates them on one branch with a final review.
implement-ticket-graph.next_step: Read the spec and blocking relationships, create the integration branch, and execute the ready frontier with bounded implementer worktrees.
implement-ticket-graph.boundary: This creates branches and worktrees, merges implementation, and resolves work through the configured tracker. It is a wider orchestration commitment.
prerequisites: An existing spec with associated dependency-linked tickets.
Configured tracker, worktree support, and parallel-agent capability.
Authorization for code, commits, integration merges, and relevant tracker updates.

alternative.when: The work is a single bounded change that does not need graph orchestration.

diagnose-fix.title: Diagnose and fix a reproducible failure
diagnose-fix.why: Its core is a fast red-capable feedback command, followed by minimization and ranked hypothesis checks.
diagnose-fix.next_step: Start by building and running one command that detects the exact reported symptom; then minimize it before testing theories.
diagnose-fix.boundary: It needs executable failure evidence. Do not claim a cause from source speculation when no meaningful feedback loop is possible.
prerequisites: The observed symptom and expected behavior.
Access to a reproducing environment or redacted artifact.
Permission to run the feedback loop and make the eventual fix.

alternative.when: A cheap local reproduction and narrow bug target are already obvious.

diagnose-live.title: Diagnose a live runtime symptom
diagnose-live.why: The Runtime forensics playbook captures a real live signal and maps a proved mechanism to source.
diagnose-live.next_step: Capture the matching CPU, heap, or UI artifact; reduce it and confirm the suspected mechanism with targeted instrumentation.
diagnose-live.boundary: The deliverable is a diagnosis, not a product fix. Instrumentation can affect a live process, so use an appropriate permitted instance.
prerequisites: Access and permission to instrument the target live process.
A matching runtime control or profiling tool available in the host.

alternative.when: You want a reproducible feedback loop and an implemented fix rather than diagnosis alone.

design-reference.title: Use a reference for interface and seam design
design-reference.why: It supplies the shared module, interface, seam, adapter, depth, and locality vocabulary.
design-reference.next_step: Map callers and dependencies, compare a few interface shapes, and state the test surface and tradeoffs without editing code.
design-reference.boundary: This is a reference for reasoning, not an autonomous coordinator. Advice alone does not authorize refactoring.
prerequisites: The module’s current or proposed callers and responsibilities.

alternative.when: You want a broader survey of recent change areas and a visual report of architectural improvement candidates.

design-prototype.title: Prototype to answer one design question
design-prototype.why: It builds throwaway logic demos or switchable UI variants whose shape follows a specific uncertainty.
design-prototype.next_step: Name the decision and the observable result that would settle it; build the smallest exploratory artifact that answers it.
design-prototype.boundary: The artifact is exploratory. Do not treat a plausible prototype as production-ready code or a validated integration.
prerequisites: A specific behavioral or interface question.
Permission to create throwaway artifacts in a suitable location.

alternative.when: You want synthesized architectural designs followed by implementation.

design-implement.title: Compare architectural shapes, then implement
design-implement.why: It grounds the surrounding system, compares structurally distinct sketches, and implements the selected design.
design-implement.next_step: Supply constraints and caller usage, compare at least two shapes, and request an explicit checkpoint if you need approval before implementation.
design-implement.boundary: Implementation is the default after synthesis. A design-only request needs a checkpoint or a narrower reference route.
prerequisites: Permission for design sketches and implementation.
Available or explicitly adapted arena and model roles.
Access to the surrounding code and constraints.

alternative.when: You want interface advice only, without implementation.

review-standards-spec.title: Report standards and specification findings
review-standards-spec.why: It pins a diff and reviews repository standards and spec compliance on separate axes.
review-standards-spec.next_step: Supply a resolving fixed point, the exact change, relevant standards, and the originating spec or an explicit absence.
review-standards-spec.boundary: The output is review findings. Missing specification coverage is reported, and review does not itself authorize code fixes or merging.
prerequisites: A nonempty diff from a valid fixed point.
Repository standards and the spec source, if available.
Support for the separate review tracks.

alternative.when: You want a synthesized adversarial judgment from diverse model reviewers rather than two separate standards/spec reports.

review-adversarial.title: Get an independent adversarial verdict
review-adversarial.why: It gives reviewers the same intent and artifact, then synthesizes their independent challenges.
review-adversarial.next_step: State the intended result, package the exact files or diff, and run the configured independent reviewers.
review-adversarial.boundary: The deliverable is a verdict. The source explicitly does not auto-apply fixes.
prerequisites: A clear intent and exact artifact to review.
Multiple suitable model reviewers available or an explicit adaptation.

alternative.when: Your priority is separate standards and spec-compliance reports.

write-pr-body.title: Write an evidence-backed PR description
write-pr-body.why: It structures the body around a small explanatory view, before/after evidence, and merge risk.
write-pr-body.next_step: Bring the finished diff, concrete validation evidence, and rollback implications; draft the body from those facts.
write-pr-body.boundary: This is a writing template. It does not make the PR merge-ready, open it, or merge it by itself.
prerequisites: A concrete change and actual before/after evidence.
Known scope and rollback implications.

alternative.when: You need a general technical-document structure rather than Matt’s specific PR-body format.

ready-pr.title: Make an existing PR ready for a merge decision
ready-pr.why: The Babysit playbook manages the merge frontier, review threads, and CI until the forge says it is merge-ready.
ready-pr.next_step: Identify the existing PR or ordered stack, select check or drive mode, and resolve the frontier’s relevant blockers.
ready-pr.boundary: Babysitting does not authorize merging. The source also limits topology changes and escalates conflicts to the owner.
prerequisites: An existing PR or ordered stack.
Forge CLI access, relevant watcher capability, and permission for scoped fixes and thread replies.
A single responsible babysitter for the stack.

alternative.when: You only need findings, without CI watching or external changes.

ship-pr.title: Verify and land an explicitly authorized PR run
ship-pr.why: The Shipping playbook requires independent per-PR runtime verdicts and lands only the contiguous verified run from the bottom.
ship-pr.next_step: Identify the explicitly authorized PR set, obtain current independent verdicts, and land only the verified bottom-up run.
ship-pr.boundary: This merges code and can retarget or move dependent branches. A green CI check alone is not its runtime verification verdict.
prerequisites: Explicit authorization to land the selected PRs.
Merge-ready PRs and independent verdicts covering their current patches.
Forge CLI and independent runtime-verification capability, with environment adaptation checked.

alternative.when: Use the Babysit playbook instead if the request ends at merge readiness.

learn-conversation.title: Learn through a code-grounded conversation
learn-conversation.why: It combines how code behaves with why it was shaped that way and builds the explanation at the learner’s pace.
learn-conversation.next_step: Name the topic and what you already understand; start with one small complete explanation and expand as needed.
learn-conversation.boundary: This teaches through conversation. It is not the persistent lesson-and-progress workspace of Matt’s teach skill.
prerequisites: A topic and, for code explanations, relevant source or evidence access.

alternative.when: You want saved lessons, resources, and evidence of progress across sessions.

learn-workspace.title: Create a persistent learning workspace
learn-workspace.why: It maintains a mission, sourced resources, HTML lessons, reference materials, and learning records across sessions.
learn-workspace.next_step: Choose the learning mission and a workspace destination, then ground the first bounded lesson in high-quality resources.
learn-workspace.boundary: This writes multiple persistent learning artifacts in the selected workspace. It has more setup than a single explanation.
prerequisites: An ongoing learning goal and writable teaching workspace.
Access to suitable learning sources.

alternative.when: You want a conversational explanation now rather than a long-lived learning workspace.

technical-document.title: Structure and clarify technical writing
technical-document.why: It chooses tutorial, how-to, reference, or explanation before refining precision and readability.
technical-document.next_step: Identify the reader’s task and choose one document mode, then revise the draft using real repository terms and verifiable claims.
technical-document.boundary: It improves document structure and language; it does not verify product behavior or justify invented evidence.
prerequisites: A target audience and document purpose.
A draft or concrete source material.

alternative.when: The document is steering instructions or a skill intended primarily for agents.

triage-requests.title: Triage requests into actionable work
triage-requests.why: It classifies and verifies requests, gathers missing decisions, and records a durable agent-ready brief.
triage-requests.next_step: Select a narrow issue set and configured triage roles; verify each request before assigning a state.
triage-requests.boundary: This changes tracker state and may post AI-labeled comments. External PR triage depends on the repository’s configuration.
prerequisites: Configured tracker and triage vocabulary.
Authorization for the selected issue reads, writes, and comments.

alternative.when: A plan is already agreed and simply needs a graph of implementation tickets.

session-retrospective.title: Find improvements to the agent’s working environment
session-retrospective.why: It inspects an actual coding session for navigation, checks, standards, tooling, and information-access improvements.
session-retrospective.next_step: Choose the session and review its primary records; return prioritized environment improvements backed by observed friction.
session-retrospective.boundary: The first deliverable is prioritized candidates, not automatic feature changes or silent edits to global instructions.
prerequisites: Access to the selected session records and repository check configuration.

alternative.when: You specifically want durable skill-edit proposals using the session’s multiple review lenses.

prevent-mistakes.title: Prevent recurring classes of agent mistakes
prevent-mistakes.why: It requires evidence of repetition and prefers structural enforcement over another instruction.
prevent-mistakes.next_step: Find a mistake class that occurred at least twice, choose architecture, types, lint, or tests, and prove the check catches a real past mistake.
prevent-mistakes.boundary: This edits the repository and commits fixes by mistake class. It is not a report-only retrospective.
prerequisites: Evidence of repeated mistakes.
Permission for repository changes, checks, and commits.

alternative.when: You want prioritized improvement candidates before authorizing structural changes.

sharpen-task.title: Improve the prompt without expanding the task
sharpen-task.why: It asks what expert methods, raw evidence, and independent correctness checks the task is missing.
sharpen-task.next_step: Supply the current task prompt; rewrite it around stronger evidence and methods while leaving the user’s decisions open.
sharpen-task.boundary: The output is a revised prompt. It does not execute the rewritten task or add unrelated scope.
prerequisites: An existing task prompt and its intended scope.

alternative.when: The underlying decisions need an interactive interview rather than a prompt rewrite.

coordinate-workers.title: Coordinate parallel coverage or candidate work
coordinate-workers.why: It declares a completion rule, bounded slices or race arms, and consolidates terminal evidence while retaining coverage gaps.
coordinate-workers.next_step: Define the artifact and done predicate, give each worker its own output, and declare how candidates or slices will be judged.
coordinate-workers.boundary: Worker agreement is not proof, and missing coverage is never a pass. Runtime, cloud, and model assumptions require host adaptation.
prerequisites: A partitionable bounded task or explicit candidate race.
Parallel-worker support and a declared selection or coverage rule.
Separate writable outputs where workers write.

alternative.when: The task first needs a custom auditable workflow because ordinary playbooks do not fit.

portable-handoff.title: Prepare a portable handoff for the next session
portable-handoff.why: It summarizes the current work for another agent, references existing artifacts, and redacts sensitive details.
portable-handoff.next_step: State what the next session is for; save a concise handoff in the OS temporary directory with artifact pointers and suggested skills.
portable-handoff.boundary: This writes a temporary handoff. It does not automatically message or launch another agent, or copy secrets into the summary.
prerequisites: The current conversation or reliable work context.
A next-session focus and writable OS temporary directory.

alternative.when: You need to reconstruct context across prior scoped chats before making the handoff.

catch-up.title: Catch up on this chat and outstanding decisions
catch-up.why: It reads changes since your last message and gives enough context to resolve every outstanding user-owned call.
catch-up.next_step: Identify your last message, inspect current touched work and PR state, and summarize changes plus the decisions that still need you.
catch-up.boundary: This is read-only catch-up. Do not start an app, edit code, or invent an action item to fill the reply.
prerequisites: Access to the current chat and state of any touched work.

alternative.when: The needed context spans earlier chats or workspaces rather than the current chat interval.
